semin-durr:25-25.t:
His saying: {بِغَيْظِهِمْ}: It is possible that the bāʾ is causal (sababiyya) — this is what Abū al-Baqāʾ expressed as "the object" (al-mafʿūl), meaning that it is a transitive-making bāʾ (muʿaddiya). The second possibility: that it is for accompaniment, in which case it is a ḥāl (circumstantial), that is, "enraged" (mughīẓīn).

His saying: {لَمْ يَنَالُواْ خَيْراً} is a second ḥāl, or a ḥāl from the first ḥāl, so that the two are nested (mutadākhila). It is also possible that it is a ḥāl from the pronoun that is genitive by iḍāfa. al-Zamakhsharī allowed that it be an explication (bayān) of the first ḥāl, or resumptive (mustaʾnafa). The explication is not evident except on the basis of badal (substitution), and the resumptive reading is remote.

semin-durr:26-26.t:
His saying: {وَأَنزَلَ الذين}: that is, "and Allah sent down". And {مِّنْ أَهْلِ الكتاب} is an explication (bayān) of the relative noun, and so is attached to an omitted element; it is also possible that it is a ḥāl (circumstantial). And «مِنْ صَياصِيْهم» is attached to «أَنْزل», and «مِنْ» marks the starting point. The word «الصَّياصِي» is the plural of «صِيْصِيَة», meaning fortresses. Anything by which one defends oneself and fortifies oneself is called a «صِيْصِيَة»; from this the horn of the bull and the spur of the cock are called «صِيْصِيَة». «الصَّياصِي» also means the weaver's thorn (shawk al-ḥāka), which is made of iron. Duraid ibn al-Ṣimma said:

3690 - ... ... ... like the falling of the iron weaver's picks on stretched-out cloth (كوَقْعِ الصَّياصِيْ في النسيجِ المُمَدَّدِ)

His saying: «فريقاً تَقْتُلون»: «فريقاً» is accusative (manṣūb) by what follows it. Likewise the second «فريقاً» is accusative by what precedes it. The sentence explains and confirms Allah's casting terror into their hearts. The majority read both verbs in the second person. Ibn Dhakwān, in one transmission, read both in the third person. al-Yamānī read the first only in the third person. Abū Ḥaywa read «تَأْسرون» with ḍamma on the sīn.

His saying: «لم تَطؤُوْها»: the sentence is an adjective (ṣifa) of «أرضاً». The majority read it with a hamza carrying ḍamma, then a quiescent wāw, as the imperfect of waṭiʾa. Zayd ibn ʿAlī read «تَطُوْها», with a wāw after a ṭāʾ carrying fatḥa. Its explanation is that he substituted an alif for the hamza, which is contrary to the regular rule, as in his saying:

3691 - Truly the lions are at ease in their lairs ... (إنَّ الأُسودَ لَتَهْدا في مَرابِضِها)

Then, when he attached it to the wāw, two quiescent letters met and the first of them was dropped, as in «لم يَرَوْها». This is better than saying that he then treated the alif substituted for the hamza as an original alif and dropped it for the jussive, because the better course there is not to drop it, out of regard for its origin. Some have cited as evidence for the dropping the saying of Zuhayr:

3692 - Bold: when he is wronged he punishes with his own wrong, swiftly; and if he is not begun upon with wrong, he does wrong (جَرِيْءٍ متى يُظْلَمْ يعاقِبْ بظلمِه ... سَريعاً وإن لا يُبْدَ بالظُّلمِ يَظْلِمِ)

semin-durr:28-28.t:
His saying: {أُمَتِّعْكُنَّ وَأُسَرِّحْكُنَّ}: The majority read both as jussive (majzūm). There are two explanations. The first: that it is jussive as the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), and what lies between the protasis and its apodosis is parenthetical (muʿtariḍ); the entry of the fāʾ upon a parenthetical sentence does no harm. Similar in the entry of the fāʾ is the poet's saying:

3693 - And know — for a man's knowledge benefits him — that everything that has been decreed will surely come (واعلَمْ فَعِلْمُ المَرْءِ يَنْفَعُه ... أَنْ سَوْفَ يَأْتيْ كلُّ ما قُدِرا)

He means: "and know that everything will surely come". The second: that the apodosis is «فَتَعالَيْنَ», and «وأُمَتِّعْكن» is the answer to this imperative.

Zayd ibn ʿAlī read «أُمْتِعْكُنَّ», with the tāʾ unshadded, from amtaʿahu. Ḥumayd al-Khazzāz read «أُمَتِّعُكُن وأُسَرِّحْكُن» in the nominative (marfūʿ) for both, as resumptive (istiʾnāf). And «سَراحاً» stands in the place of «التَّسْريح» (the verbal noun).

semin-durr:30-30.t:
His saying: {مَن يَأْتِ مِنكُنَّ}: The majority read «يَأْتِ» with a yāʾ (with two dots below), construing it according to the form (lafẓ) of «مَنْ». Zayd ibn ʿAlī, al-Jaḥdarī and Yaʿqūb read it with a tāʾ (with two dots above), construing it according to its meaning, because the feminine sense is reinforced by the words «منكُنَّ»; and «منكنَّ» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the agent of «يَأْتِ». The reading of «مُبَينة» with respect to kasra or fatḥa of the yāʾ has already been given in Sūrat al-Nisāʾ.

His saying: «يُضاعَفْ»: Abū ʿAmr read «يُضَعَّفْ» with a yāʾ (dots below) and a shadda on the ʿayn carrying fatḥa, in the passive; «العذابُ» is nominative because it stands in the place of the agent (nāʾib fāʿil). Ibn Kathīr and Ibn ʿĀmir read «نُضَعِّفْ» with the nūn of majesty and a shadda on the ʿayn carrying kasra, in the active; his saying «العذابَ» is accusative as direct object (mafʿūl bihi). The rest read «يُضاعَفْ», from the form mufāʿala, in the passive; «العذابُ» is nominative because it stands in the place of the agent. The explanation of taḍʿīf and muḍāʿafa has already been given in Sūrat al-Baqara, which makes repeating it unnecessary.

semin-durr:31-31.t:
His saying: {وَتَعْمَلْ صَالِحاً نُؤْتِهَآ}: The two (al-Akhawān, Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī) read «ويَعْمَلْ ويُؤْتِ» with a yāʾ (dots below) in both. The rest read «وتَعْمل» with a tāʾ (dots above) and «نُؤْتِها» with a nūn. As for the yāʾ in «ويَعْمَلْ», it is for construing according to the form of «مَنْ», which is the basic rule. The tāʾ is according to its meaning, since what is meant by it is feminine; this is reinforced by the preceding feminine word «مِنْكُنَّ». Similar is the saying:

3694 - And among women there is one who is a garden ... (وإنَّ مِن النِّسْوان مَنْ هي روضةٌ ...)

When "among women" came first, the sense was preferred, so he construed according to it. As for «يُؤْتِها» with a yāʾ (dots below), the pronoun refers to Allah the Exalted, because He was mentioned before in «لله ورسوله». With the nūn, it is the nūn of majesty, and there is in it a shift from the third person to the first.

al-Jaḥdarī, Yaʿqūb, Ibn ʿĀmir in one transmission, Abū Jaʿfar and Shayba read «تَقْنُتْ» with a tāʾ (dots above), construing according to the meaning, and likewise «وتَعْمَل». Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "Some of them read «ومَنْ تَقْنُتْ» with the feminine, construing according to the meaning, and «يَعْمَلْ» with the masculine, construing according to the form." He said: "Some of the grammarians said: this is weak, because the masculine is the basic form, so it is not made to follow the feminine. But what they gave as their reason has a parallel in the Quran. The Exalted said: {خَالِصَةٌ لِّذُكُورِنَا وَمُحَرَّمٌ على أَزْوَاجِنَا} [al-Anʿām: 139]."

semin-durr:34-34.t: His saying: {مِنْ آيَاتِ الله}: an explication (bayān) of the relative noun, and so it is attached to «أعني» ("I mean"). It is also possible that it is a ḥāl (circumstantial), either from the relative noun or from its omitted returning pronoun, and then it is likewise attached to an omitted element.

semin-durr:35-35.t: His saying: {والحافظات}: its object is omitted because what indicates it has preceded. The implied form is "and the women who guard them (fully)". Likewise «والذاكراتِ». The omission is made pleasing by the verse-endings (fawāṣil). And the masculine is given precedence over the feminine in «لهم», and he did not say «ولَهُنَّ».

semin-durr:36-36.t:
His saying: {أَن يَكُونَ}: it is the subject (ism) of kāna, and the predicate (khabar), the preposition and its genitive noun, is advanced. His saying {إِذَا قَضَى الله} may be a pure adverb (ẓarf) governed by the "being established" (al-istiqrār) to which the predicate is attached, that is: "it was not established for any believing man or believing woman, at the time of Allah's decree, that they have a choice"; or it may be conditional, with its apodosis implied, indicated by the preceding negation.

The Kufans and Hishām read «يكونَ» with a yāʾ (dots below), because «الخِيَرَة» is feminine only figuratively (majāzī), and also because of the separation. The rest read it with a tāʾ (dots above), regarding its form. It has already been mentioned that «الخِيَرَة» is the verbal noun of takhayyara, like «الطِّيَرَة» from taṭayyara. ʿĪsā ibn Sulaymān reported that it was read «الخِيْرَة» with a quiescent yāʾ. And «مِنْ أمرِهم» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «الخِيَرة»; it was also said that «مِن» means "in". The pronoun in «أمرِهم» and what follows is plural because what is meant by "believing man" and "believing woman" is the class (jins), and the masculine is given precedence over the feminine. al-Zamakhsharī said: "The pronoun by rights should have been singular, as you say: 'No man or woman came to me but that such-and-such was his affair.'" The Shaykh (Abū Ḥayyān) said: "That is not correct, because the conjunction is with wāw, so that is not permissible except by interpreting an omission."

semin-durr:37-37.t:
His saying: {أَمْسِكْ عَلَيْكَ}: Some grammarians stated explicitly that «على» in a construction like this is a noun. He said: "so that a verb acting on an attached pronoun does not pass over to its own attached pronoun, except in the chapter of ẓanna and in the two words faqada and ʿadima." And he counted among that:

3699 - Take it easy; for matters, their measures are in the hand of the Divine (هَوِّنْ عليكَ فإنَّ الأمورَ ... بكفِّ الإِلهِ مقاديرُها)

Likewise he ruled on «عَنْ» in his saying:

3700 - Leave aside the booty that was shouted about in its courtyards ... (دَعْ عنك نَهْباً صِيْحَ في حُجُراتِهِ ...)

You have already had this at length in al-Naḥl, in His saying {وَلَهُمْ مَّا يَشْتَهُونَ} [al-Naḥl: 57], and in His saying {وهزى إِلَيْكِ بِجِذْعِ} [Maryam: 25] and {واضمم إِلَيْكَ جَنَاحَكَ} [al-Qaṣaṣ: 32].

His saying: «وتُخْفي»: there are several explanations. The first: that it is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to «أَمْسِكْ», that is: "when you were combining your saying such-and-such with hiding such-and-such, and fearing the people." al-Zamakhsharī said this. The second: that it is the wāw of ḥāl (circumstantial), that is: "you say such-and-such in this state." al-Zamakhsharī said this too. There is a point to consider in it, since it is an affirmative imperfect, so how can the wāw come directly before it? Its analysis is like that of «قمتُ وأَصُكُّ عينَه» ("I rose and I strike his eye"), I mean by implying a subject (mubtadaʾ). The third: that it is resumptive (mustaʾnaf). al-Ḥawfī said this. As for His saying {والله أَحَقُّ أَن تَخْشَاهُ}, its like has already been given in Barāʾa.

His saying: «وَطَراً»: the object of «قَضَى». «الوَطَر» is desire and love; al-Mubarrad said this. And he recited:

3701 - How could my stay in Medina be, after Jamīl ibn Maʿmar had fulfilled his need of it (وكيف ثَوائي بالمدينةِ بعدَما ... قَضَى وَطَراً منها جميلُ بنُ مَعْمَرِ)

Abū ʿUbayda said: "«الوَطَر» is the need and the want." And he recited for al-Ḍubayʿ al-Fazārī:

3702 - He bade us farewell before we could bid him farewell, when he had fulfilled a need of our youth (ودَّعَنا قبلَ أَنْ نُوَدِّعَهْ ... لَمَّا قضى مِنْ شبابِنا وَطَراً)

The majority read «زوَّجْناكها». ʿAlī and his two sons al-Ḥasan and al-Ḥusayn, may Allah be pleased with them and make them pleased, read «زَوَّجْتُكَها» with the tāʾ of the first person singular.

And «لِكَيْلا» is attached to «زَوَّجْناكها», and here «كي» only governs the subjunctive, because the preposition has entered upon it. The two pronouns are attached to the verb because they differ in rank.

semin-durr:38-38.t: His saying: {سُنَّةَ الله}: accusative (manṣūb) as a maṣdar (verbal noun), like {صُنْعَ الله} [al-Naml: 88] and {وَعْدَ الله} [al-Nisāʾ: 122]; or a noun put in the place of the maṣdar; or accusative by "He made" (jaʿala); or by ighrāʾ (urging), that is: "so upon him is the sunna of Allah." Ibn ʿAṭiyya said this. The Shaykh (Abū Ḥayyān) rejected it, because the governor of ighrāʾ is not omitted, and because it would be urging a third person (ighrāʾ al-ghāʾib). What has occurred of it is interpreted as rare, such as: «عليه رجلاً لَيْسَني». I say: His saying, peace be upon him, has occurred: «وإلاَّ فعليه بالصوم» ("otherwise let him fast"). It was said: this is ighrāʾ. It was also said that it is not, but is rather a mubtadaʾ and khabar, with the bāʾ redundant in the mubtadaʾ. That is an analysis whose meaning is invalid, because fasting is not obligatory upon that person.

semin-durr:39-39.t: His saying: {الذين يُبَلِّغُونَ}: it is possible that it follows «الذين خَلَوْا» (as an adjective), and possible that it is cut off from it, in the nominative or the accusative, by implying "they" (hum), or "I mean" (aʿnī), or "I praise" (amdaḥu).

semin-durr:40-40.t:
His saying: {ولكن رَّسُولَ الله}: The majority read «لكن» with the shadda dropped, and «رسول» accusative. Its accusative case is either by implying "kāna", as the earlier "kāna" indicates it, that is "but he was", or by conjunction (ʿaṭf) to «أبا أَحَدٍ».

The first is more fitting, because «لكن» is not a conjunction, on account of the wāw; so it is more fitting that it enter upon sentences, like the one that is not a conjunction.

Abū ʿAmr, in one transmission, read it with the shadda, so that «رسولَ الله» is its subject (ism), and its predicate is omitted as indicated, that is: "but the Messenger of Allah is he", that is, Muḥammad. The omission of its predicate is common. And it was recited:

3707 - Had you been of Ḍabba you would have known my kinship, but (you are) a Zanjī with big lips (فلو كنتَ ضَبِّيَّاً عَرَفْتَ قَرابتي ... ولكنَّ زَنْجِيَّاً عظيمَ المَشافِرِ)

that is: "you". They also transmit this verse as «ولكنَّ زَنْجيٌّ» in the nominative, as evidence for the omission of its subject, that is: "but you".

Zayd ibn ʿAlī and Ibn Abī ʿAbla read it without the shadda and with «رسولُ» nominative as a mubtadaʾ, its khabar implied, that is: "he"; or the reverse, that is: "but he is a messenger", like the saying:

3704 - I am not the vain poet among them, but a champion of the harsh war (ولَسْتُ الشاعرَ السَّفسافَ فيهمْ ... ولكنْ مِدْرَهُ الحربُ العَوانِ)

that is: "but I am the champion".

His saying: «وخاتم»: ʿĀṣim read it with fatḥa on the tāʾ, and the rest with kasra. The fatḥa is a noun for the instrument with which one seals, like «الطابَع» and «القالَب» for that with which one stamps and moulds; this is the well-known view. Abū al-Baqāʾ mentioned other possibilities for it, among them that it has the sense of a maṣdar. He said: "This is how it is mentioned in some works of iʿrāb." I say: this is an outright mistake; how could it be otherwise, when it requires figurative usage and an implied element? Had this been said of «خاتِم» with kasra it would have been nearer, because a maṣdar may come on the pattern fāʿil and fāʿila. That is coming shortly. Among them also: that it is a noun meaning "last". Among them: that it is a past verb like qātala, in which case «النبيين» is the direct object. I say: the reading of ʿAbd Allah, «خَتَم النبيين», supports this.

The kasra is on the basis that it is an active participle, and the reading of ʿAbd Allah mentioned above supports it. Some said: it has the same meaning as the fatḥa, that is, it means "the last of them".

semin-durr:43-43.t: His saying: {وَمَلاَئِكَتُهُ}: it is either conjoined (ʿaṭf) to the agent of «يُصَلِّي», and the separation by the preposition and its genitive noun makes emphasis by a pronoun unnecessary. This is according to those who hold shared meaning (ishtirāk), or a common core meaning, or figurative usage, since the ṣalāh of Allah the Exalted is not the same as their ṣalāh; or it is a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is omitted, that is: "and His angels pray". This is according to those who consider any of the preceding permissible; but there is a point of investigation in it, namely that they stated explicitly that when the meanings of the two predicates differ, it is not permissible to omit one because of the other, even if the wording is the same. So you do not say «زيد ضاربٌ وعمروٌ» meaning "and ʿAmr is striking in the land", that is, travelling.

semin-durr:44-44.t: His saying: {تَحِيَّتُهُمْ}: it may be a maṣdar annexed to its object, and it may be annexed to its agent and its object, in the sense that some of them greet others. So the pronoun may be for the agent and the object under two considerations, not that it is agent and object from a single aspect, as said by one who said, regarding {وَكُنَّا لِحُكْمِهِمْ شَاهِدِينَ} [al-Anbiyāʾ: 78], that it is annexed to both the agent and the object.

semin-durr:45-45.t: His saying: {شَاهِداً}: an anticipated (muqaddara) ḥāl (circumstantial), or a concurrent one because of the nearness of the time.

semin-durr:46-46.t:
His saying: {بِإِذْنِهِ}: a ḥāl (circumstantial), that is: "accompanied by His facilitating"; he does not mean actual permission, because that is understood from «أَرْسلْناك».

His saying: «وسِراجاً»: it may be conjoined to what came before, either on the basis of comparison, or on the basis of an omitted muḍāf, that is: "possessor of a lamp". al-Farrāʾ allowed that the original was "and reciting a lamp" (tāliyan sirājan); by "lamp" he means the Quran. On this it would be a conjunction of attributes that belong to a single person, because the reciter is the one sent. al-Zamakhsharī allowed that it be conjoined to the object of «أَرْسَلْنَاك». There is a point to consider in that, because the lamp is the Quran, and it is not described as being sent (irsāl) but as being sent down (inzāl); unless it is said that it was construed according to the meaning, as in:

3705 - I fed it chopped straw and cold water ... (عَلَفْتُها تِبْناً وماءً بارداً ...)

Also, in secondary elements things are tolerated that are not tolerated in primary ones.

semin-durr:48-48.t: His saying: {وَدَعْ أَذَاهُمْ}: it is possible that «أذاهم» is annexed to its object, that is: "leave your harming of them", meaning your punishing them; and it is possible that it is annexed to its agent, that is: "leave what they harmed you with, and do not take them to account until you are commanded."

semin-durr:49-49.t:
His saying: {ثُمَّ طَلَّقْتُمُوهُنَّ}: If it is asked: what is the point of bringing «ثم», when the ruling for a woman divorced immediately after the contract is the same? The answer: it follows the usual case. al-Zamakhsharī said: "It removes the supposition from anyone who might suppose a difference of ruling between divorcing her when the marriage is recent and when the marriage is long past and the period has extended with her in the husband's care before he divorces her." The Shaykh (Abū Ḥayyān) said: "He used ʿasā as the ṣila of «مَنْ», and that is not permissible." I say: his statement can be analysed as the poet's saying is analysed:

3706 - I am one who casts a glance toward the one whom — perhaps, even if her abode is far — I shall visit (وإني لَرامٍ نَظْرَةً قِبَلَ التي ... لَعَلِّي وإنْ شَطَّتْ نَواها أَزورها)

and that is by implying "saying" (iḍmār al-qawl).

His saying: «تَعْتَدُّوْنَها» is an adjective (ṣifa) of «عِدَّة». «تَعْتَدُّونها» is on the form tafʿalūnahā (iftiʿāl): either from al-ʿadad (number) or from al-iʿtidād, that is: "you count it" or "you complete its number", from your saying "ʿadda the dirhams and iʿtaddahā", meaning he completed their number, like "I measured it (kiltuhu) and he measured it out (iktālahu)" and "I weighed it (wazantuhu) and he weighed it out (ittazanahu)". Ibn Kathīr, in one transmission, and the people of Mecca read it with the dāl unshadded. There are two explanations for it. The first: that it is from al-iʿtidād, and they disliked its doubling so they lightened it. al-Rāzī said this; he said: "Had it been from al-iʿtidāʾ, which is wrongdoing, it would be weak, because al-iʿtidāʾ takes «على»." It was said: it may be from al-iʿtidāʾ with the preposition omitted, that is: "you transgress against it", that is, against the ʿidda, figuratively, and then «تَعْتَدُوْنها», as in the saying:

3707 - She yearns and shows what is in her of longing, and I hide that which, but for grief, would have finished me (تَحِنُّ فَتُبْدِيْ ما بها مِنْ صَبابةٍ ... وأُخْفي الذي لولا الأسى لقَضاني)

that is, "would have finished me" (laqaḍā ʿalayya). al-Zamakhsharī said: "It was also read «تَعْتَدُونها» unshadded, that is: 'you transgress in it' (taʿtadūna fīhā)", as in the saying:

3708 - And many a day we witnessed ... ... ... (ويومٍ شَهِدْناه ...)

the verse. What is meant by al-iʿtidāʾ is what is in His saying: {وَلاَ تُمْسِكُوهُنَّ ضِرَاراً لِّتَعْتَدُواْ} [al-Baqara: 231]. He means that he omitted the preposition, as it is omitted in his saying:

And many a day we witnessed, Sulaymā and ʿĀmir, few but for the thrust and the thirsty spears are its supererogatory gains (ويومٍ شَهِدْناه سُلَيْمى وعامِراً ... قليلٍ سوى الطَّعْنِ النِّهالِ نوافِلُهْ)

It was also said: the meaning of «تَعْتَدُونها» is "you transgress against them in it". Ibn ʿAṭiyya denied the reading as from Ibn Kathīr and said: "Ibn Abī Bazza made a mistake in transmitting it from him." It is not as he said. The second: that it is from al-ʿudwān and al-iʿtidāʾ, whose explanation has already been given; and the objection of Abū al-Faḍl to it, that it ought to take «على», whose answer has also been given. al-Ḥasan read «تَعْدُّونها» with a quiescent ʿayn and a shadda on the dāl, which combines two quiescent letters not in accordance with their two limits.

semin-durr:50-50.t:
His saying: {مِمَّآ أَفَآءَ}: an explication (bayān) of «مَلَكَتْ»; this is not a restriction, for even if his right hand had acquired her by purchase the ruling would be the same; it came out following the usual case.

His saying: «وامرأةً»: the majority read it accusative. There are two explanations. The first: that it is conjoined to the object of «أَحْلَلْنا», that is: "and We made lawful for you a woman described by these two conditions." Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "A group rejected this and said: «أَحْلَلْنا» is past, while «إنْ وَهَبَتْ», which is an adjective of the woman, is future; so «أَحْلَلْنا» is in the position of its apodosis, and the apodosis of a condition cannot be past in meaning." He said: "That is not correct, because the meaning of 'making lawful' here is informing of the lawfulness if the act occurs on that basis, as you say: 'I have permitted you to speak to so-and-so if he greets you.'" The second: that it is accusative by an implied verb, its implied form being: "and He makes lawful for you a woman."

His saying: «إنْ وَهَبَتْ ... إنْ أرادَ»: this is the interposing of a condition upon a condition, and the second is a restriction on the first; for that reason we parse it as a ḥāl (circumstantial), because the ḥāl is a restriction. For this reason the jurists stipulated that the second must precede the first in existence. So if he said: "If you eat, if you ride, you are divorced", then the riding must precede the eating. This is so that the quality of being a ḥāl and the restriction are realised as I mentioned to you; for were it not to precede, some part of the eating would be left unrestricted by riding, and so they stipulated that the second precede. The verification of this has passed, and that it is on condition that there is no indication preventing the second from preceding the first, as in your saying: "If I marry you, if I divorce you, my slave is free": here the precedence of divorce over marriage cannot be conceived.

However, a difficulty has occurred to me concerning what the jurists said, on the basis of this verse. It is that the second condition here cannot precede in existence with respect to the ruling specific to the Prophet ﷺ — not that it is impossible rationally. For the exegetes interpreted His saying «إنْ أرادَ» as meaning "if he accepted the gift", because by his acceptance, peace be upon him, his marriage is completed; and its precedence over the gift cannot be conceived, since acceptance comes later. Moreover the story was as I mentioned, that his desire came after her gift, and this is mentioned in the exegesis. The Shaykh (Abū Ḥayyān), when he came to this place, made the second condition precede the first by the general rule and did not find any of what I mentioned problematic. I presented this difficulty to a number of the notables of our time and they acknowledged it, and no answer to it appeared, except what I stated earlier, that there is an indication preventing that, as I exemplified for you just now.

Abū Ḥaywa read «وامرأة» nominative as a mubtadaʾ, the khabar implied, that is: "We have made her lawful for you also." In His saying {إِنْ أَرَادَ النبي} there is a shift (iltifāt) from the second person to the third using the overt noun, to alert that the reason for that is prophethood; then he returned to the second person and said: «خالصةً لك».

Ubayy, al-Ḥasan and ʿĪsā read «أَنْ» with fatḥa, and there are two explanations. The first: that it is a badal (substitute) of «امرأة», a badal of inclusion (badal ishtimāl); Abū al-Baqāʾ said this. It is as if it were said: "and We made lawful for you a woman's giving herself to you." The second: that it is by omission of the lām of cause, that is: "because she gave." Zayd ibn ʿAlī read «إذ وَهَبَتْ», which has the sense of causation.

His saying: «خالصةً»: the majority read it accusative. There are several explanations. The first: that it is accusative as a ḥāl from the agent of «وَهَبَتْ», that is: "in the state of her being exclusive to you, to the exclusion of others." The second: that it is a ḥāl from «امرأةٌ» because it was described and so became specified; it is the same as the first in meaning. al-Zajjāj took this view. The third: that it is an adjective of an implied maṣdar, that is: "an exclusive gift", and he made it accusative by «وَهَبَتْ». The fourth: that it is a confirmatory maṣdar like {وَعْدَ الله} [al-Nisāʾ: 122]. al-Zamakhsharī said: "The fāʿil and fāʿila forms among maṣdars are not rare, such as «الخارِج», «القاعِد», «الكاذِبة» and «العافِية»." By «الخارج» he means what is in the saying of al-Farazdaq:

3709 - ... ... nor a false word coming out of my mouth (... ولا خارِجاً مِنْ فِيَّ زُوْرُ كَلامِ)

and by «القاعد» what is in their saying «أقاعِداً وقد سار الرَّكْبُ» ("sitting while the caravan has set out?"), and by «الكاذبة» what is in His saying the Exalted {لَيْسَ لِوَقْعَتِهَا كَاذِبَةٌ}. The Shaykh (Abū Ḥayyān) objected to his saying "not rare" and said: "Rather they are rare, and what has occurred is interpreted otherwise." It was also read «خالِصَةٌ» nominative. If «خالصةً» is a ḥāl, the mubtadaʾ «she» is implied, that is, the woman who gives herself; and if it is a maṣdar, it is implied: "that state is exclusive." And «لك» is an explication (bayān), that is: "I mean for you", like "may there be rain for you" (saqyan laka).

His saying: «لكيلا» is attached to «خالصةً», with what is between them parenthetical, and «مِنْ دون» is attached to «خالصةً», as you say: "it became free of such-and-such" (khalaṣa min kadhā).

semin-durr:51-51.t:
His saying: {وَمَنِ ابتغيت}: two explanations are possible for «مَنْ». The first: that it is conditional, in the position of accusative by what follows it. And His saying {فَلاَ جُنَاحَ عَلَيْكَ} is its apodosis. The meaning: "whichever of the women you set aside you seek, then there is no blame upon you in that." The second: that it is a mubtadaʾ with its returning pronoun omitted. On this «مَنْ» may be a relative noun, or may be conditional, and {فَلاَ جُنَاحَ عَلَيْكَ} is the khabar or the apodosis, that is: "and the one you sought." In that case a pronoun returning to the conditional noun is needed in the apodosis, that is: "in seeking her and asking for her." It was also said: in the speech a conjoined element is omitted, its implied form being: "and whomever you seek, of those you set aside and those you did not set aside, are equal; there is no blame upon you", as you say: "whoever of those who met you and those who did not meet you, all of them are grateful to you", meaning: whoever met you and whoever did not meet you. In this there is obscurity.

His saying: «ذلك»: that is, the delegation to your will is nearer to the comfort of their eyes.

The majority read «تَقَرَّ» in the active, with «أَعْيُنُهُنَّ» as its agent. Ibn Muḥayṣin read «تُقِرَّ», from aqarra, the quadriliteral; its agent is the second-person pronoun, and «أعينَهُنَّ» is accusative as direct object.

It was also read «تُقَرَّ» in the passive, with «أعينهُنَّ» nominative because it stands in the place of the agent. The meaning of "coolness of the eye" (qurrat al-ʿayn) has already been given in Maryam.

His saying: «كلُّهن»: the majority read it nominative as emphasis (tawkīd) of the agent of «يَرْضَيْن». Abū Unās read it accusative as emphasis of the object of «آتيتهُنَّ».

semin-durr:52-52.t:
His saying: {لاَّ يَحِلُّ}: Abū ʿAmr read «تَحِلُّ» in the feminine, regarding the form (lafẓ); the rest read it with the yāʾ, because it is a class term and also because of the separation.

His saying: «مِنْ بَعْدُ»: that is, after those whose lawfulness We specified for you. This has already been given. It was also said: after the permission of Muslim women, to the exclusion of women of the People of the Book.

His saying: «مِنْ أزواجٍ»: a direct object, and «مِنْ» is redundant in it, to cover the whole class.

His saying: «ولو أعجبكَ»: like the saying «أَعْطُوا السائل ولو على فَرَس» ("Give the beggar, even if on a horse"), that is: in every state, even in this contrary state.

His saying: «إلاَّ ما مَلَكَتْ»: there are several explanations. The first: that it is an exception from «النساء», and then two explanations are possible: accusative, on the basic rule of exception, and nominative as a badal, which is the preferred one. The second: that it is an exception from «أزواج»; Abū al-Baqāʾ said this. It may then be in the position of accusative on the basic rule of exception, or in the position of genitive as a badal of «هنَّ» by form, or in the position of accusative as a badal of «هُنَّ» by position.

Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "If «ما» is a maṣdar then it is in the position of accusative, because it is not of the same kind." This is not good, because he said afterwards: "and the implied form is: 'except what the right hand possesses' (milk al-yamīn), and milk means 'possessed' (mamlūk)." End. And if it has the meaning of "possessed" it becomes of the same kind, and if it becomes of the same kind it is not a disconnected exception (munqaṭiʿ). Even supposing it is disconnected, its accusative is not necessary; rather, according to Tamīm, nominative as a badal is permissible, and accusative on the basic rule as in the connected exception, on the condition that the governor can validly be directed to it, as I have verified more than once. Here the governor can be directed to it; but the well-known dialect is that of the Hijaz: the accusative is obligatory in the disconnected exception absolutely, as Abū Muḥammad mentioned just now.

semin-durr:53-53.t:
His saying: {إِلاَّ أَن يُؤْذَنَ}: there are several explanations. The first: that it is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial), its implied form being: "except accompanied by permission." The second: that it is on the omission of the bāʾ of cause, its implied form being: "except by reason of permission being given to you", as in the saying «فاخْرُجْ به», meaning "by reason of it." The third: that it is accusative as an adverb (ẓarf). al-Zamakhsharī said: "«إلاَّ أَنْ يُؤْذَنَ» has the sense of an adverb, its implied form being: 'except at the time of permission being given to you'. And «غيرَ ناظرين» is a ḥāl from «لا تَدْخُلوا». The exception applies to the ḥāl and the time together, as if it were said: 'Do not enter the houses of the Prophet except at the time of permission, and do not enter except not looking out for its readiness (ināhu)'."

The Shaykh (Abū Ḥayyān) rejected the first, on the ground that the grammarians stated explicitly that the maṣdar «أنْ» does not occupy the position of an adverb. It is not permissible to say: "I will come to you when the cock crows" using «أَنْ يصيحَ الديك», even though that is permissible with an explicit maṣdar, as in "I will come to you at the crowing of the cock." He rejected the second on the ground that after «إلاَّ» in exception only the excepted, or that from which the exception is made, or its attribute, may occur. Anything other than this is not permissible according to the majority. al-Kisāʾī and al-Akhfash allowed that, and they allowed «ما قام القومُ إلاَّ يومَ الجمعة ضاحِكِين» ("The people did not rise except on Friday, laughing").

And «إلى طعامٍ» is attached to «يُؤْذَنَ», because it has the sense: "except that you are invited to a meal." The majority read «غيرَ ناظرين» accusative as a ḥāl, as stated; according to al-Zamakhsharī and those who follow him the governor of it is «يُؤْذَنَ», while according to others the governor is an implied one, its implied form being: "enter not looking out." Ibn Abī ʿAbla read «غيرِ» genitive as an adjective of «طعام». People considered this weak because the pronoun is not made to appear, since it refers to someone other than the one it belongs to; so it ought to have been said: «غيرَ ناظرين إناه أنتم». This is the opinion of the Basrans. The Kufans allow that if there is no ambiguity, as in this verse. This question and its branches and what was said about it have already been given. Is that restricted to the noun, or does it also apply to the verb? A well-known disagreement, which few control.

The majority read «إناه» in the singular, that is, its being cooked. It is said: anā al-ṭaʿām inan, like qalāhu qilan. al-Aʿmash read «آناءه» as a plural on the pattern afʿāl, in which the second hamza was changed to an alif and the yāʾ to a hamza because it came at the end after an extra alif, so that in pronunciation it is like «آناء» in His saying {وَمِنْ آنَآءِ الليل} [Ṭā Hā: 130], although the meaning differs.

His saying: «ولاَ مُسْتَأْنِسِين»: it may be accusative, conjoined to «غيرَ», that is: "do not enter it not looking, nor making yourselves at home." It was also said: this is conjoined to an anticipated ḥāl, that is: "do not enter abruptly, nor making yourselves at home"; and it may be genitive, conjoined [to] «ناظرين», that is: "not looking and not making yourselves at home."

His saying: «لحديثٍ»: the lām may be the lām of cause, that is: "making yourselves at home in order that you talk to one another"; or it may be the lām that strengthens the governor, because it is secondary (a derived form), that is: "nor making yourselves at home with the talk of the household or others."

His saying: «إنَّ ذلكم»: that is, "your waiting and your making yourselves at home"; the two were indicated with the demonstrative for a single thing, as in His saying {عَوَانٌ بَيْنَ ذلك} [al-Baqara: 68], that is: what has been mentioned. It was also read «لا يَسْتَحِي» with a single yāʾ, the other being omitted. They differed as to whether the omitted one is the first or the second. This was given in al-Baqara, and that it is a transmission from Ibn Kathīr. It is the dialect of Tamīm. They say: istaḥā yastaḥī, like istaqā yastaqī. I recited there what was heard on this.

His saying: «أَنْ تُؤْذُوا»: it is the subject (ism) of kāna, and «لكم» is the predicate. And {وَلاَ أَن تنكحوا} is conjoined to the subject of kāna. And «أبداً» is an adverb.

semin-durr:55-55.t: [His saying]: {واتقين}: conjoined to an omitted element, that is: "comply with what you have been commanded, and fear (Allah)."

semin-durr:56-56.t: His saying: {وَمَلاَئِكَتَهُ}: the majority read it accusative, as a conjunction (nasaq) to the subject (ism) of «إنَّ». And «يُصَلُّون»: is it a khabar for Allah and His angels, or for the angels only, with the khabar for the Majestic Name omitted because the two prayers differ? A disagreement given shortly before. Ibn ʿAbbās read, and it was also transmitted from Abū ʿAmr, «وملائكتُه» nominative. It may then be conjoined to the position of the subject of «إنَّ», according to some; or it may be a mubtadaʾ with its khabar omitted, which is the school of the Basrans. A discussion of this has already been given, in the manner of «زيدٌ ضاربٌ وعمرٌو», meaning "striking in the land".

semin-durr:57-57.t: His saying: {يُؤْذُونَ الله}: there are several explanations. That is: they say about Him what has the form of harm, even though no injury from that reaches Him, glory be to Him the Exalted, since they describe Him with what does not befit His majesty, such as taking rivals and attributing a child and a wife to Him. Or it may be on the omission of a muḍāf, that is: "the friends of Allah" (awliyāʾ Allah). It was also said: the Majestic Name was brought for magnification, and what is meant is: "they harm My Messenger", like His saying the Exalted {إِنَّمَا يُبَايِعُونَ الله} [al-Fatḥ: 10].

semin-durr:58-58.t: His saying: {فَقَدِ احتملوا}: the khabar of «والذين». The fāʾ entered because the relative noun resembles a condition.

semin-durr:59-59.t:
His saying: {يُدْنِينَ}: like His saying {قُل لِّعِبَادِيَ ... يُقِيمُواْ} [Ibrāhīm: 31]; and «مِنْ» is partitive.

His saying: «ذلك أَدْنَى»: that is, the drawing down of the cloaks is nearer to their being recognised, and hence to their not being harmed.

semin-durr:60-60.t: His saying: {إِلاَّ قَلِيلاً}: that is: "except for a short time", or "except a short neighbourhood". It was also said: «قليلاً» is accusative as a ḥāl from the agent of «يُجاوِرونك», that is: "except as a few, abased ones", in the sense of "few". It was also said: «قليلاً» is accusative as the excepted, that is: "none of them will be your neighbour except a few of them, in the most abject and fewest state."

semin-durr:61-61.t:
His saying: {مَّلْعُونِينَ}: a ḥāl from the agent of «يُجاوِرونك»; Ibn ʿAṭiyya, al-Zamakhsharī and Abū al-Baqāʾ said this. Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "because it means 'they will be expelled from it accursed'." al-Zamakhsharī said: "The particle of exception entered upon the ḥāl and the adverb together, as passed in His saying {إِلاَّ أَن يُؤْذَنَ لَكُمْ إلى طَعَامٍ غَيْرَ} [al-Aḥzāb: 53]." I say: the Shaykh's (Abū Ḥayyān's) discussion with him has already been given, and it applies again here. al-Zamakhsharī allowed it to be accusative as an expression of reproach (shatm). Ibn ʿAṭiyya allowed it to be a badal of «قليلاً» on the basis that it is a ḥāl, as its explanation was given earlier. It is also possible that «مَلْعونين» is an adjective of «قليلاً», on the basis that it is accusative as the excepted from the wāw of «يُجاوِرُوْنَك», as its explanation was given earlier, that is: "none of them will be your neighbour except a few, accursed." It is also possible that it is accusative by «أُخِذُوا», which is the apodosis. This is according to al-Kisāʾī and al-Farrāʾ, since they allow the object of the apodosis to be advanced before the conditional particle, as in «خيراً إْن تَأْتِني تُصِبْ» ("good, if you come to me you will obtain").

al-Zamakhsharī prevented this and said: "It is not correct for it to be accusative by «أُخِذُوا», because what follows the conditional word does not act upon what precedes it." This is walking on the well-trodden path from him. His saying "what follows the conditional word" includes the protasis verb and the apodosis. As for the apodosis, its ruling has been given; as for the protasis, al-Kisāʾī also allowed advancing its object before the particle, as in «زيداً إنْ تَضْرِبْ أُهِنْكَ» ("Zayd, if you strike (him), I will humiliate you"). So three positions are summarised on the question: prohibition absolutely; permission absolutely; and a distinction: it is permissible to advance it as the object of the apodosis and not permissible to advance it as the object of the protasis, which is the opinion of al-Farrāʾ.

His saying: «وقُتِّلوا»: the majority read it with shadda. It was also read without shadda. The latter is refuted by the maṣdar coming on the form taqtīl, unless it is said that it came on other than its expected form. And His saying «سُنَّةُ اللَّهِ»: its like has already been given.

semin-durr:63-63.t: His saying: {لَعَلَّ الساعة}: the apparent view is that «لعلَّ» suspends (the verb's action) as the expression of wishing (tamannī) suspends it. And «قريباً» is the khabar of kāna on the omission of a described noun, that is: "something near". It was also said: the implied form is "the arrival of the Hour" (qiyām al-sāʿa), so the Hour was regarded in the feminine of «تكون», and the omitted muḍāf was regarded in the masculine of «قريباً». It was also said: «قريباً» has become frequently used as adverbs are used, so here it is an adverb in the position of the khabar.

semin-durr:65-65.t: His saying: {فِيهَآ}: that is, in the blaze (al-saʿīr), because it is feminine, or because it has the sense of Jahannam. And «لا يَجِدُون» is a second ḥāl (circumstantial), or a ḥāl from «خالدين».

semin-durr:66-66.t: His saying: {يَوْمَ}: governed by «خالدين», or by «يَجدون», or by «نصيراً», or by «اذْكُرْ» ("remember"), or by «يقولون» after it. The majority read «تُقَلَّبُ» in the passive; «وجوهُهم» is nominative as the one whose agent is not named. al-Ḥasan, ʿĪsā and al-Ruʾāsī read «تَقَلَّبُ» with fatḥa on the tāʾ, that is: "turn over"; «وجوهُهم» is its agent. Abū Ḥaywa read «نُقَلِّبُ» with a nūn, that is: "We"; «وجوهَهم» is accusative. ʿĪsā of Basra read «تُقَلِّبُ» with ḍamma on the tāʾ and kasra on the lām, that is: the blaze turns over, or the angels do; «وجوهَهم» is accusative as direct object. «يقولون» is a ḥāl, and «يا لَيْتَنا» is the quoted speech.

semin-durr:67-67.t: His saying: {سَادَتَنَا}: Ibn ʿĀmir and others read it as a plural with alif and tāʾ («ساداتنا»). The rest read «سادَتنا» on the basis that it is a broken plural not pluralised with alif and tāʾ. Then «سادة» may be a plural of «سَيِّد», but it is not regular, because the form fayʿil is not pluralised on faʿala, and «سادَة» is faʿala, since the origin is «سَوَدَة». It may also be a plural of «سائد», like fājir and fajara, kāfir and kafara; and this is nearer to regularity than the former. Ibn ʿĀmir pluralised this a second time with alif and tāʾ, which is also not regular, like «بيُوتات» and «جِمالات».

semin-durr:68-68.t: ʿĀṣim read «كبيراً» with the single-dotted bāʾ (kabīran); the rest read it with the three-dotted thāʾ (kathīran). Their two meanings have been given in al-Baqara.

semin-durr:69-69.t: His saying: {عِندَ الله}: the majority read «عند» as a figurative adverbial. Ibn Masʿūd, al-Aʿmash and Abū Ḥaywa read «عَبْداً» (a servant), from servitude (ʿubūdiyya), with «لله» as a preposition and its genitive noun; and it is a good reading. Ibn Khālawayh said: "I prayed behind Ibn Shannabūdh in Ramaḍān and heard him reading with this reading of Ibn Masʿūd." I say: he, may Allah have mercy on him, was fond of reporting irregular readings, and his story with the vizier Ibn Muqla and with Ibn Mujāhid in that matter is well known. And «ما» in «ممَّا قالُوا» is either a maṣdar or has the sense of "that which" (alladhī).

semin-durr:72-72.t:
And His saying: {إِنَّا عَرَضْنَا}: either literal, or a representation and imagining (tamthīl wa-takhyīl).

And His saying: «فَأَبَيْنَ»: he brought its pronoun as the feminine plural pronoun, because a broken plural of non-rational beings allows that even if it is masculine. I mention it only so that it is not supposed that he gave the feminine, «السماوات», precedence over the masculine, «الجبالُ».

semin-durr:73-73.t: His saying: {لِّيُعَذِّبَ}: attached to his saying «وحَمَلها». It was said: it is the lām of consequence (ṣayrūra), because he did not carry it for that purpose. It was also said: it is the lām of cause used figuratively, since it was the result of his carrying that, it was made like the motivating cause. al-Aʿmash read «ويتوبُ» nominative, as resumptive.

semin-durr:32-32.t:
His saying: {كَأَحَدٍ مِّنَ النسآء}: al-Zamakhsharī said: "«أَحَد» in origin has the sense of waḥad, which is 'one'. Then it was put into the general negation, in which the masculine, the feminine, the single and what is beyond are alike. The meaning: 'You are not like one group of the groups of women', that is: if you search out the groups of women one by one, no single group of them will be found that equals you in merit and precedence. Of this is His saying {والذين آمَنُواْ بالله وَرُسُلِهِ وَلَمْ يُفَرِّقُواْ بَيْنَ أَحَدٍ مِّنْهُمْ} [al-Nisāʾ: 152]; he means between one group of them, treating all of them equally in that they are on the clear truth." The Shaykh (Abū Ḥayyān) said: "As for his saying that «أحد» in origin has the sense of waḥad, which is 'one', that is correct. But his saying 'it was put' up to his saying 'and what is beyond' is not correct, because the one used in general negation has a meaning different from the meaning of 'one' (wāḥid); for wāḥid applies to everything described by oneness, whereas aḥad used in general negation is specific to rational beings. The grammarians mentioned that its root is hamza, ḥāʾ, dāl, while the root of «أحد» in the sense of 'one' is wāw, ḥāʾ, dāl; so they differ in root and in meaning. As for his saying 'you are not like one group', we have said that its meaning is that none of you individually is such. So he ruled on each one, not on the whole as a whole. As for {وَلَمْ يُفَرِّقُواْ بَيْنَ أَحَدٍ مِّنْهُمْ} [al-Nisāʾ: 152], it is possible that it is the one used in general negation; for that reason it came in the context of negation and so was general, and betweenness (bayniyya) is suited to generality. It is also possible that «أحد» has the sense of 'one', and a conjoined element was omitted, that is: 'between one and one', as he said:

3695 - There was not between al-Khayr, had Abū Ḥujur come safe, and me, but a few nights (فما كان بينَ الخيرِ لو جاء سالماً ... أبو حُجُرٍ إلاَّ ليالٍ قَلائِلُ)

that is: between al-Khayr and me." End. I say: as for his saying that they differ in meaning and root, that is granted. But al-Zamakhsharī did not make the aḥad whose origin is wāḥid the same as the aḥad specific to negation, and it does not prevent the aḥad whose origin is wāḥid from occurring in the context of negation. The difference between them is only this: the one whose hamza is original is not used except in negation, like its sisters ʿarīb, katīʿ, wābir and tāmir; while the one whose origin is wāḥid may be used in affirmation and negation. The difference between them is also that the one specific to negation is inert (jāmid), while this one is a descriptive form. Also, the one specific to negation is specific to rational beings, while this is not specific. As for the meaning of the negation, it is apparent as al-Zamakhsharī said, in ruling on the whole; but the meaning as the Shaykh said is clearer, though it is contrary to the apparent view.

His saying: «إنِ اتَّقَيْتُنَّ»: there are two explanations for its apodosis. The first: that it is omitted, as what precedes it indicates it, that is: "if you fear Allah, then you are not like any one of them." So the condition is a restriction on the negation of their being likened to any one of the women. The second: that its apodosis is His saying «فلا تَخْضَعْنَ», and taqwā is on its usual sense. On this the Shaykh allowed that ittaqā may mean "to face", that is: "if you face anyone, do not soften your speech to him." And ittaqā in the sense of "to face" is known in the language. And he recited:

3696 - The veil fell and she did not mean to drop it, so she took it up and faced us with her hand (سَقَطَ النَّصِيفُ ولم تُرِدْ إسقاطَه ... فتناوَلَتْهُ واتَّقَتْنا باليَدِ)

that is: and faced us with her hand. He said: "This meaning would be more far-reaching in praising them, since it does not make their merit depend on taqwā, nor on His forbidding them to be submissive by it; for they are fearful of Allah the Exalted in themselves. The conditional construction, in its apparent sense, requires that they are not adorned with taqwā."

I say: this is leaving the apparent sense without necessity. As for the verse, the ittiqāʾ is also on its usual sense, that is, she protected her face with her hand from us.

His saying: «فَيَطْمَعَ»: the majority read it accusative, as the answer to the prohibition. al-Aʿraj read it jussive, with kasra on the ʿayn because of the meeting of two quiescent letters. It was transmitted from him, and from Abū al-Sammāl, Ibn ʿUmar and Ibn Muḥayṣin, with fatḥa on the yāʾ and kasra on the mīm. This is anomalous, in that the past and the imperfect agree in vowel. It was also transmitted from al-Aʿraj that he read with ḍamma on the yāʾ and kasra on the mīm, from aṭmaʿa. It admits two explanations. The first: that the agent is a latent pronoun returning to the submission (al-khuḍūʿ); the one with sickness in his heart. It is also possible that «الذي» is the agent, with its object omitted, that is: "so that the sick one makes himself covet."

His saying: «وَقَرْنَ»: Nāfiʿ and ʿĀṣim read with fatḥa on the qāf. The rest read it with kasra. As for the fatḥa, it is in two ways. The first: that it is an imperative from qarirtu — with kasra on the first rāʾ — fī al-makān, aqarru bihi with fatḥa. So two rāʾs met in «اقْرَرْنَ», and the second was dropped for lightness, and the vowel of the first rāʾ was transferred to the qāf, and the hamzat al-waṣl was dropped as no longer needed, so it became «قَرْن». Its pattern on this basis is faʿna, for the omitted one is the lām, because the heaviness came about through it. It was also said: the omitted one is the first rāʾ, because when its vowel was transferred it remained quiescent, with another quiescent one after it, so the first was dropped because of the meeting of two quiescent letters; its pattern on this basis is falna, for the omitted one is the ʿayn. Abū ʿAlī said: "The first rāʾ was replaced by a yāʾ and its vowel transferred to the qāf, so two quiescent letters met, and the yāʾ was dropped because of their meeting." These are three explanations for the view that it is an imperative from qarirtu bi-al-makān.

The second explanation: that it is an imperative from qāra yaqāru, like khāfa yakhāfu, when it gathers together. Of this is «القارَة» for its gathering. So the ʿayn was dropped because of the meeting of two quiescent letters, and it was said «قَرْنَ» like «خَفْنَ». Its pattern on this basis is also falna.

However, some people spoke against this reading in two respects. The first: Abū Ḥātim said: it is said qararu bi-al-makān with fatḥa, aqirru bihi with kasra, and qarrat ʿaynuhu with kasra, taqarru with fatḥa; so how can «وَقَرْنَ» be read with fatḥa? The answer to this: that both fatḥa and kasra have been recorded in each of the two; Abū ʿUbayd related it. That was already given in Sūrat Maryam.

The second: granted that it is said qarirtu bi-al-makān with kasra, aqarru bihi with fatḥa, and that the imperative from it is «اقْرَرْنَ», there is nothing to justify the omission, because the fatḥa is light; and it cannot be modelled on their saying «ظَلْتُ» and its chapter, because there are two heavy things there: the doubling and the kasra, so the omission is good, whereas here there is only the doubling.

The answer: that what calls for the omission is only the repetition. This is supported by the fact that they did not omit despite repetition and the presence of ḍamma, though it is heavier, as in «اغْضُضْنَ أبصارَكنَّ», and that would have been more fitting for omission, so that it would be said «غُضْنَ»; but what is heard is contrary to it. The Exalted said {وَقُل لِّلْمُؤْمِنَاتِ يَغْضُضْنَ مِنْ أَبْصَارِهِنَّ} [al-Nūr: 31]. Although the Shaykh Jamāl al-Dīn ibn Mālik said: "It is omitted in this case a fortiori"; or you may say that this reading is only from qāra yaqāru in the sense of "gathered together". It is a good explanation free of artificiality, and the objection of Abū Ḥātim and others is repelled, were it not that the meaning is a command to remain settled, not to gather.

As for the kasra, it is also in two ways. The first: that it is an imperative from qarra bi-al-makān with fatḥa in the past and kasra in the imperfect, which is the eloquent dialect, and the three explanations mentioned first apply to it: either dropping the second rāʾ or the first, or replacing it with a yāʾ and dropping it, as al-Fārisī said. There is no objection to this reading because it comes on the well-known usage, so Abū Ḥātim's objection is repelled; and because kasra is heavy, so the second objection is repelled; and its meaning corresponds to what is meant by it, firmness and settlement.

The second explanation: that it is an imperative from waqara yaqiru, that is, "was firm and settled". Of this is al-waqār (dignity). Its origin is «اِوْقِرْن», then the fāʾ, which is the wāw, was dropped, and the hamzat al-waṣl dispensed with, leaving «قِرْن». This is exactly like the imperative of waʿada. Its pattern on this basis is ʿilna. These explanations mentioned are found only by one who is practised in the science of taṣrīf; otherwise he is hard pressed by them.

His saying: «تَبَرُّجَ الجاهليةِ»: a comparative maṣdar, that is, "like the displaying of". al-Tabarruj is appearing, from al-burj (tower), for its being visible; this has been given. al-Bazzī read «ولا تَّبَرَّجْنَ» with assimilation of the tāʾ into the tāʾ. The rest drop one of them. Its verification was given in al-Baqara at «ولا تَيَمَّموا».

His saying: «أهلَ البيتِ»: there are several explanations: the vocative and specification (ikhtiṣāṣ), except that it is less common in the second person than in the first. It was heard: «بك اللَّهَ نرجو الفضلَ» ("in You, O Allah, we hope for bounty"), though it is more common in the first person, as in her saying:

3697 - We are the daughters of Ṭāriq; we walk upon the cushions (نحن بناتِ طارِقْ ... نَمْشِي على النمارِقْ)

[and his saying]:

3698 - We, the Banū Ḍabba, are the people of the camel; death is sweeter to us than honey (نحن بني ضَبَّةَ أصحابُ الجملْ ... الموتُ أَحْلَى عندنا من العَسَلْ)

and «نحن العربَ أَقْرَى الناسِ للضيف» ("we Arabs are the most hospitable of people to the guest") and «نحن معاشرَ الأنبياءِ لا نورث» ("we, the company of prophets, are not inherited from"); or it may be on praise, that is: "I praise the People of the House."

semin-durr:2-2.t:
In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.
His saying: {بِمَا تَعْمَلُونَ خَبِيراً}, and shortly after it {بِمَا تَعْمَلُونَ بَصِيراً} [al-Aḥzāb: 9]: Abū ʿAmr read both with the yāʾ of the third person. The others read them with the tāʾ of address, and both are clear. As for the third person in the first, it is because of His saying «الكافرين» and «المنافقين»; as for the address, it is because of His saying {يا أَيُّهَا النبي}, since he and his community are meant, or he was addressed in the plural out of reverence, as in his saying:
3675 - فإنْ شِئْتَ حَرَّمْتُ النساءَ سِواكُمُ ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
(If you wish, I will forbid [myself] women other than you ...)
The Shaykh allowed it to be an iltifāt, meaning away from the absent disbelievers and hypocrites; that is remote. As for the third person in the second, it is because of His saying {إِذْ جَآءَتْكُمْ} [al-Aḥzāb: 9]; as for the address, it is because of His saying {ياأيها الذين آمَنُوا} [al-Aḥzāb: 9].

semin-durr:4-4.t:
His saying: {اللائي}: the Kufans and Ibn ʿĀmir read it with a sukūn-vowelled yāʾ after a kasra-vowelled hamza. This is the original form of this word, because it is a plural of «التي» in meaning. Abū ʿAmr and al-Bazzī read «اللاَّيْ» with a sukūn-vowelled yāʾ in connected speech after a pure alif, in one of their two ways; they have another way, which will come.
The basis of this reading is that they omitted the yāʾ after the hamza for lightness, then replaced the hamza with yāʾ and made it quiescent because it had become a yāʾ preceded by a kasra, like the yāʾ of «القاضي» and «الغازي»; except that this is not analogical, for the analogical course is to make the hamza intermediate (bayna bayna). Abū ʿAlī said: "One does not proceed to such a substitution unless it is heard." I say: Abū ʿAmr ibn al-ʿAlāʾ said: "It is the dialect of Quraysh in which people were commanded to recite." Some said: they did not substitute; rather they wrote it so, and the reciters expressed it as a substitution. That is nothing.
Abū ʿAlī and others said: "Abū ʿAmr's clear pronunciation of «اللايْ يَئِسْنَ» shows that he softens and does not substitute." This is not necessary, because the substitution is incidental; therefore he did not assimilate. These two [Abū ʿAmr and al-Bazzī] and Warsh also read it with a hamza softened to the intermediate. Some claimed that nothing else is sound from them, and it is an analogical lightening; when they pause they make the hamza quiescent, and whenever they make it quiescent its softening to the intermediate becomes impossible due to the loss of its vowel, so it is turned into yāʾ because it occurs quiescent after a kasra, and it is not their school to lighten it so as to leave it as a hamza.
Qunbul and Warsh read it with a kasra-vowelled hamza without yāʾ; they omitted the yāʾ and made do with the kasra in its place. This very disagreement runs also in al-Mujādila and al-Ṭalāq.
His saying: «تُظاهِرون»: ʿĀṣim read «تُظاهِرون» with ḍamma on the tāʾ and kasra on the hāʾ after an alif, the imperfect of «ظاهَرَ». Ibn ʿĀmir read «تَظَّاهرون» with fatḥa on the tāʾ and hāʾ and a doubled ẓāʾ, the imperfect of «تَظاهَر»; the origin is «تتظاهرون» with two tāʾs, which was assimilated. The two brothers [Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī] likewise, except that they lightened the ẓāʾ; the origin is also with two tāʾs, but they omitted one of them. These are two ways of lightening this kind: either assimilation or omission. Its thorough treatment has preceded in the like of «يَذَّكَّرْ» and «تَذَكَّرُون», doubled and lightened. The like of it has also preceded in al-Baqara.
The others read «تَظَّهَّرون» with fatḥa on the tāʾ and hāʾ and doubled ẓāʾ and hāʾ without alif. The origin: «تَتَظَهَّرُوْن» with two tāʾs, which was assimilated like «تَذَكَّرون». All read in al-Mujādila as they read here in His saying {يُظَاهِرُونَ مِن نِّسَآئِهِمْ} [al-Mujādila: 3], except the two brothers, who differed there from their own origin here, and read in al-Mujādila with a doubled ẓāʾ like the reading of Ibn ʿĀmir. Ẓihār is derived from «الظَّهْر» ("the back"). Its origin is that a man says to his wife: "You are to me like my mother's back." The two brothers did not read with lightening in al-Mujādila because there is no justification for it, namely the omission; for the omission was only because two identical letters met, the two tāʾs, while in al-Mujādila there is a yāʾ (from below) and a tāʾ (from above), so two identical letters do not meet, hence no omission, and assimilation was unavoidable.
This is what was read by mass transmission (mutawātir).
Ibn Waththāb read «تُظْهِرُون» with ḍamma on the tāʾ, sukūn on the ẓāʾ and kasra on the hāʾ, the imperfect of «أَظْهَرَ». From him also «تَظَهَّرُون» with fatḥa on the tāʾ and a lightened ẓāʾ and a doubled hāʾ; the origin is «تَتَظَهَّرون», the imperfect of «تَظَهَّر» doubled, with one of the two tāʾs omitted. Al-Ḥasan read «تُظَهِّرون» with ḍamma on the tāʾ, fatḥa on the lightened ẓāʾ and a doubled kasra-vowelled hāʾ, the imperfect of «ظَهَّر» doubled. From Abū ʿAmr: «تَظْهَرُون» with fatḥa on the tāʾ and hāʾ and sukūn on the ẓāʾ, the imperfect of «ظهر» lightened. Ubayy read, and it is thus in his codex, «تَتَظَهَّرون» with two tāʾs. These are nine readings: four mutawātir and five anomalous. The derivation of these verbs from the word «الظَّهْر» is like the derivation of «لَبَّى» from «التَّلْبية» and of «تَأَفَّفَ» from «أُفٍّ». It is made transitive with «مِنْ» only because it contains the sense of distancing, as if it were said: "they distance themselves from their wives because of ẓihār", as was mentioned regarding the transitivity of īlāʾ with «مِنْ» in al-Baqara.
His saying: «ذلكمْ قولُكم»: mubtadaʾ and khabar, that is, your calling the adopted ones sons is a mere utterance of the tongue without reality. «الأَدْعياءُ» is the plural of «دَعِيّ» in the sense of «مَدْعُوّ» ("called"), faʿīl in the sense of mafʿūl. Its origin is «دَعِيْوٌ», which was assimilated; but its plural on «أَدْعِياء» is not analogical, because the pattern afʿilāʾ is the plural of faʿīl with a weak lām only when it is in the sense of fāʿil, like «تقِيّ» and «أَتْقِياء», «غَنيّ» and «أغنياء»; this, although it is a faʿīl with a weak lām, is in the sense of mafʿūl, so the analogical plural would be on faʿlā, like «قتيل» and «قَتْلَى», «جريح» and «جَرْحى». A parallel in irregularity is their saying «أَسير» and «أُسَراء», while the analogical is «أَسْرَى», and the original has also been heard in it.

semin-durr:5-5.t:
His saying: {هُوَ أَقْسَطُ}: that is, their calling [them] by their fathers' names; the maṣdar is implied because its verb points to it, as in His saying {اعدلوا هُوَ أَقْرَبُ} [al-Māʾida: 8].
His saying: {ولكن مَّا تَعَمَّدَتْ}: two views are possible for «ما». The first: it is genitive in position, conjoined to the preceding «ما» which is governed by «في», the implied form being "but the blame is in what your hearts intended". The second: it is nominative in position as a mubtadaʾ, with the khabar omitted, its implied form being "you are held to account for it", or "upon you in it is blame", or the like.

semin-durr:6-6.t:
His saying: {وَأَزْوَاجُهُ أُمَّهَاتُهُمْ}: that is, like their mothers in ruling. It is also possible that the comparison be forgotten and they be made their mothers by way of exaggeration.
His saying: «بعضُهم»: two views are possible. The first: it is a badal from «أُوْلُو». The second: it is a mubtadaʾ and what follows it is its khabar, and the sentence is the khabar of the first.
His saying: {فِي كِتَابِ الله}: it may be attached to «أَوْلَى», because the elative (afʿal al-tafḍīl) governs the adverbial. It may also be attached to an omitted element as a ḥāl from the pronoun in «أَوْلَى», and the governing element in it is «أَوْلَى» because it resembles the adverbial. It cannot be a ḥāl from «أُوْلُو», because of the separation by the khabar, and because there is no governing element in it.
His saying: «من المؤمنين»: two views are possible. The first: it is the «مِنْ» that governs the thing surpassed, like the one in «زيدٌ أفضلُ من عمروٍ» ("Zayd is better than ʿAmr"); the meaning: "those related by blood are more entitled to inheritance than the believers and the unrelated emigrants". The second: it is explicative, brought to explain "those related by blood", so it is attached to an omitted element, that is, "I mean"; the meaning: "those related by blood among the believers are more entitled to inheritance than strangers".
His saying: {إِلاَّ أَن تفعلوا}: this is an exception of a different kind (istithnāʾ min ghayr al-jins), excepted from the meaning and drift of the discourse, since the implied form is: "those related by blood are closer to one another in inheritance and otherwise; but if you do good to others among your allies, that is yours." «تَفْعَلوا» is made transitive by «إلى» because it contains the sense of "you go in to".

semin-durr:7-7.t:
His saying: {وَإِذْ أَخَذْنَا}: two views are possible. The first: it is accusative by «اذكر», that is, "and remember when We took". The second: it is conjoined to the position of «في الكتاب», so «مَسْطُوراً» governs it, that is, "this ruling was written in the Book and at the time of Our taking".
His saying: «ميثاقاً غليظاً»: it is the first [covenant], repeated only for the additional description and to announce its emphasis.

semin-durr:8-8.t:
His saying: {لِّيَسْأَلَ}: two views on it. The first: it is the lām of purpose, that is, "We took their covenant so that He may ask the believers about their truthfulness and the disbelievers about their denial", and it dispensed with the second by mentioning its consequence, namely His saying «وأَعدَّ». The second: it is the lām of consequence, that is, "He took the covenant from the prophets so that matters may come to such-and-such". The object of «صدقِهم» is omitted, that is, "their truthfulness to their covenant". It is also possible that «صِدْقِهم» be in the sense of «تَصْديقهم» ("their confirming"), and its object is also omitted, that is, "about their confirming the prophets".
His saying: «وأَعَدَّ»: two views. The first: it is conjoined to what «ليَسْألَ الصادقين» points to, since the implied form is: "so He rewarded the truthful and prepared for the disbelievers". The second: it is conjoined to «أَخَذْنا», because the meaning is that Allah the Exalted stressed to the prophets the call to His religion in order to reward the believers, and prepared for the disbelievers. It was also said: He omitted from the second what He affirmed its counterpart in the first, and from the first what He affirmed its counterpart in the second. The implied form: "so that He may ask the truthful about their truthfulness and so rewarded them, and ask the disbelievers about what they answered their messengers with, and prepared for them a painful punishment".

semin-durr:9-9.t: His saying: {إِذْ جَآءَتْكُمْ}: it may be accusative by «نعمةَ», that is, "the favour occurring at that time". It may also be accusative by «اذكروا» as a badal al-ishtimāl from «نعمة».

semin-durr:10-10.t:
His saying: {إِذْ جَآءُوكُمْ}: a badal from the first «إذ». Al-Ḥasan read «الجَنود» with fatḥa on the jīm; the majority read it with ḍamma. And «جنوداً» is conjoined to «ريحاً». And «لم تَرَوْها» is an adjective of them. It is reported from Abū ʿAmr and Abū Bakra [read] «لم يَرَوْها» with the yāʾ of the third person.
His saying: «الحَناجرَ»: the plural of «حَنْجَرة», which is the head of the ghalṣama; the ghalṣama is the end of the ḥulqūm; and the ḥulqūm is the passage of food and drink. It was also said: the ḥulqūm is the passage of breath, and the marī is the passage of food and drink, which is beneath the ḥulqūm. Al-Rāghib said: "The head of the ghalṣama from the outside."
And His saying: «الظنونا»: Nāfiʿ, Ibn ʿĀmir and Abū Bakr read it with the alif after the nūn of «الظُّنونا», and likewise the lām of «الرسول» in His saying {وَأَطَعْنَا الرسولا} [al-Aḥzāb: 66] and the lām of «السَّبيل» in His saying {فَأَضَلُّونَا السبيلا} [al-Aḥzāb: 67], in connected speech and in pause, in agreement with the orthography, because they are written so in the codex. Moreover this alif resembles the hāʾ of pause (hāʾ al-sakt) for showing the vowel, and the hāʾ of pause is retained in pause because of the need for it. It has been retained in connection, treating connection like pause, as has preceded in al-Baqara and al-Anʿām. So too this alif. Abū ʿAmr and Ḥamza read it with omission in both states, because it has no root. Their saying "the verse-endings were treated like rhyme-endings" is not to be relied on, because rhyme-endings generally require pause on them, while verse-endings do not require that, so they are not likened to them. The others retain it in pause and omit it in connection, treating the verse-endings like rhymes in the retention of the alif of release (alif al-iṭlāq), as in his saying:
3676 - اسْتأثَرَ اللَّهُ بالوفاءِ وبال ... عَدْلِ ووَلَّى المَلامَةَ الرَّجُلا
(Allah reserved for Himself faithfulness and justice, and left the blame to the man.)
and his saying:
3677 - أقِلِّي اللومَ عاذلَ والعِتابا ... وقُولي إن أَصَبْتُ لقد أصابا
(Lessen the blame, O reproacher, and the reproach, and say, if I am right: "He has hit the mark.")
and because it is like the hāʾ of pause, which is retained in pause and lightened in connection. I say: they say it so, likening verse-endings to rhymes, and I do not like this expression, for it is objectionable in wording, and there is no disagreement about His saying {وَهُوَ يَهْدِي السبيل} [al-Aḥzāb: 4] that it is without alif in both states.
His saying: «هنالك»: accusative by «ابْتُلِيَ»; it was also said, by «تَظُنُّون», and Ibn ʿAṭiyya considered that weak. There are two views on it. The more apparent: it is an adverb of a distant place, that is, "in that slippery place", which is the trench. The second: it is an adverb of time, and some recited in support of that:
3678 - وإذا الأمورُ تَعاظَمَتْ وتشاكَلَتْ ... فهناك يَعْتَرفون أين المَفْزَعُ
(When matters grow grave and confused, then they admit: where is the refuge?)
His saying: «وزُلْزِلُوا»: the majority read it with ḍamma on the first zāy and kasra on the second, on the original form of the passive. More than one reported from Abū ʿAmr kasra on the first; and al-Zamakhsharī reported from him an admixture of kasra (ishmām). The basis of this reading is that he made the first zāy follow the second in kasra and did not count the quiescent letter, because it is not a strong barrier, like their saying «مِنْتِن» with kasra on the mīm, while the origin is ḍamma.
His saying: «زِلْزالاً»: a maṣdar specifying the kind by description. The majority read it with kasra on the zāy. ʿĪsā and al-Jaḥdarī put fatḥa on it. They are two dialectal forms in the maṣdar of the doubled verb when it comes on the pattern fiʿlāl, like «زِلْزال», «قِلْقال» and «صِلْصال». The fatḥa form may be meant as an active participle, like «صَلْصال» in the sense of «مُصَلْصِل» and «زَلزال» in the sense of «مُزَلْزِل».

semin-durr:13-13.t:
His saying: {ياأهل يَثْرِبَ}: Yathrib is the name of Medina. Its being diptote is either for definiteness and the verbal pattern, or for definiteness and feminine gender. As for «يَتْرَب» with a two-dotted tāʾ and fatḥa on the rāʾ, it is another place. He said:
3679 -. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... مواعيدَ عُرْقوبٍ أخاه بيَتْرَبِ
(... the promises of ʿUrqūb to his brother at Yatrab.)
His saying: {لاَ مُقَامَ لَكُمْ}: Ḥafṣ read it with ḍamma on the mīm; Nāfiʿ and Ibn ʿĀmir also read it with ḍamma on its mīm in al-Dukhān in His saying {إِنَّ المتقين فِي مَقَامٍ} [al-Dukhān: 51]; and there is no disagreement that the first is with fatḥa, namely {وَمَقَامٍ كَرِيمٍ} [al-Dukhān: 26]. The others read with fatḥa on the mīm in both places. The ḍamma and fatḥa are understood from Sūrat Maryam at His saying {خَيْرٌ مَّقَاماً} [Maryam: 73]. His saying: «عَوْرَةٌ»: that is, "possessing an exposed side"; it was also said: exposed to the thief. The poet said:
3680 - له الشَّدَّةُ الأُوْلى إذا القِرْنُ أَعْورا ...
(His is the first charge when the opponent is exposed.)
Ibn ʿAbbās, Ibn Yaʿmar, Qatāda, Abū Rajāʾ, Abū Ḥaywa and others read «عَوِرة» with kasra on the wāw, and likewise {وَمَا هِيَ بِعَوْرَةٍ}; it is an active participle. It is said «عَوِر المنزلُ يَعْوَر عَوْراً وعَوْرَة فهو عَوِر وبيوتٌ عَوْرَةٌ». Ibn Jinnī said: "Keeping the wāw sound is anomalous", meaning where it is vowelled and what precedes it has fatḥa, yet it was not turned into an alif. There is something to consider in that, because the condition for that in the noun derived from the verb is that its verb be weak, like «مَقام» and «مَقال». As for this, its verb is sound, like «عَوِر». The verb was kept sound although it has the requirement for weakening, for another reason: that it is in the sense of what is not weakened, namely «أَعْوَر»; therefore no wonder is expressed from «عَوِر» and its category. «أَعْوَرَ المنزلُ»: its exposed side appeared; «أَعْوَرَ الفارسُ»: a gap appeared in him for the strike. The poet said:
3681 - متى تَلْقَهم لم تَلْقَ في البيتِ مُعْوِراً ... ولاَ الضيفَ مَسْجوراً ولا الجارَ مُرْسَلاً
(Whenever you meet them, you will not find in the house one exposed, nor the guest ill-treated, nor the neighbour left to himself.)

semin-durr:14-14.t:
His saying: {مِّنْ أَقْطَارِهَا}: «الأَقْطار» is the plural of «قُطْر» with ḍamma on the qāf, meaning a region. There is a dialectal form in it: «قُتْر» and «أَقْتار» with tāʾ. «القُطْر» also means a side. From it: «قَطَرْتُه», that is, "I threw him on his side, so he fell («تَقَطَّر»), that is, fell upon it". The poet said:
3682 - قد عَلِمَتْ سَلْمى وجاراتُها ... ما قَطَّر الفارسَ إلاَّ أنا
(Salmā and her neighbours know that none threw the horseman down but I.)
In the proverb: «الانفضاض يقطر الحلب» ("dispersal brings on milking"); its explanation: when people disperse, that is, their provisions run out, they need to milk the camels. The rain-drop (qaṭr) is called qaṭr for its falling.
His saying: «ثم سُئِلوا»: Mujāhid read «سُوْيِلُوا» with a quiescent wāw then a kasra-vowelled yāʾ, like «قُوتلوا». Abū Zayd reported «هما يَتَساوَلان» with wāw. Al-Ḥasan read «سُوْلُوا» with only a quiescent wāw, which admits two views. [The first]: its origin is «سُئِلوا» like the majority, then the kasra was lightened and so made quiescent, like their saying in «ضَرِب» with kasra, «ضَرْب» with sukūn; so the hamza became quiescent after a ḍamma and was turned into wāw, like «بُوْس» for «بُؤْس». The second: it is from the dialect of the wāw. It was transmitted from Abū ʿAmr that he read «سِيْلُوا» with a quiescent yāʾ after a kasra, like «مِيْلُوا».
His saying: «لأَتَوْها»: Nāfiʿ and Ibn Kathīr read it with the short vowel, in the sense of "they would have resorted to it and been shrouded in it". The others read it with the long vowel, in the sense of "they would have given it". Its second object is omitted, its implied form being «لآتَوْها السَّائلين» ("they would have given it to the askers"). The meaning: if you entered the houses or the city from all its sides, then its people were asked for sedition, they would not refuse to give it. The reading with the long vowel entails the reading with the short vowel, but not vice versa, in this specific meaning.
His saying: «إلاَّ يَسِيراً»: that is, "except a delay" or "except a short time". Likewise His saying {إِلاَّ قَلِيلاً} [al-Aḥzāb: 16], that is, "except an enjoyment" or "except a little time".

semin-durr:15-15.t: His saying: {لاَ يُوَلُّونَ}: an answer to His saying «عاهَدوا», because it is in the sense of «أَقْسَموا» ("they swore"). It came by reporting the wording, so it came in the third person; had it come by reporting the meaning, it would have been said «لا يُوَلِّي». The first object is omitted, that is, "they will not turn their backs to the enemy". Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "It is also read with a doubled nūn and omission of the wāw, to emphasize the answer to the oath." I say: I think this is only an error by him, for either it is read together with the negating «لا» or with the lām of emphasis. The first is not permissible, because the imperfect negated with «لا» is not emphasized by the nūn except rarely, which is not to be used as a model. The second is corrupt in meaning.

semin-durr:16-16.t:
His saying: {إِن فَرَرْتُمْ}: its apodosis is omitted because the negation before it indicates it, or it is fronted according to one who holds that.
His saying: {وَإِذاً لاَّ تُمَتَّعُونَ}: «إذن» is a response and a consequence. When it occurred after a conjunction it came in the more frequent way, which is its not governing, and what was anomalous in al-Isrāʾ was not anomalous here, so it was not read in the accusative. The majority read «تُمَتَّعون» in the second person. It was also read in the third person.

semin-durr:17-17.t:
His saying: {مَن ذَا الذي}: it has preceded in al-Baqara. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "If you say: how was mercy made the counterpart of evil in protection, when there is no protection except from evil? I say: its meaning is «أو يصيبكم بسوءٍ إنْ أرادَ بكم رحمةً» ('or He afflicts you with evil if He wills mercy for you'), so the discourse was abbreviated and run in the manner of his saying:
3683 -. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... مُتَقَلِّداً سَيْفاً ورُمْحاً
(... girded with a sword and [carrying] a spear.)
or the second was carried on the first, because of the sense of prevention in protection." The Shaykh said: "As for the first view, it contains the omission of a sentence for which no necessity calls; the second is the [better] view, especially if an omitted muḍāf is supposed, that is, «يَمْنَعُكم مِنْ مراد الله» ('He prevents you from what Allah wills')." I say: where is the second from the first, even if omission of sentences accompanies it?

semin-durr:18-18.t: His saying: {هَلُمَّ}: the discussion of it has preceded at the end of al-Anʿām. It is intransitive here and transitive there, for it governs its object in the accusative, namely «شُهداءَكم», in the sense of "bring them"; and here it is in the sense of "come" and "approach". Al-Zamakhsharī's statement here suggests that it is also transitive, with its object omitted, for he said: «وهلمُّوا إلينا», that is, "bring yourselves near to us". He said: "It is a sound by which a transitive verb was named, like «أحضِرْ» and «قَرِّب»." In his naming it a sound there is something to consider, since the onomatopoeic nouns (asmāʾ al-aṣwāt) are limited and this is not among them.

semin-durr:19-19.t:
His saying: {أَشِحَّةً}: the majority read it in the accusative. There are two views on it. The first: it is accusative for reproach (shatm). The second: as a ḥāl. As for its governing element, there are several views. The first: «ولا يأتون»; said by al-Zajjāj. The second: «هلمَّ إلينا»; said by al-Ṭabarī. The third: an implied «يُعَوِّقُون»; said by al-Farrāʾ. The fourth: «المُعَوِّقين». The fifth: «القائلين». These last two views were rejected on the ground that they contain separation between the parts of the ṣila by an extraneous element. In the rejection there is something to consider, because what separates the parts of the ṣila is from its attachments. The rejection is apparent only on the fourth view, because it has been conjoined to the relative noun before the completion of its ṣila; so consider it, for it is fine. As for «ولا يأتُون», it is parenthetical, and the parenthetical does not prevent that.
Ibn Abī ʿAbla read «أَشِحَّةٌ» in the nominative as the khabar of an implied mubtadaʾ, that is, "they are stingy". «أشحَّة» is the plural of «شَحيح», and it is a plural not subject to analogy, since the analogical plural of the descriptive faʿīl whose ʿayn and lām come from one root is afʿilāʾ, like «خليل» and «أَخِلاَّء», «ظَنين» and «أَظِنَّاء», «ضَنين» and «أَضِنَّاء». «أشِحَّاء» has been heard, and it is the analogical. «الشُّحُّ» is miserliness, which has preceded in Āl ʿImrān.
His saying: «يَنْظُرون»: in the position of ḥāl from the object of «رَأَيْتَهم», because the seeing is by sight.
His saying: «تَدُورُ»: either a second ḥāl, or a ḥāl from «يَنْظُرون».
His saying: «كالذي يُغْشَى»: three views are possible. The first: it is a ḥāl from «أعينُهم», that is, "their eyes revolve, resembling the eye of one who is fainting from death". The second: it is an adjective of a maṣdar supposed for His saying «يَنْظُرون», the implied form being "they look at you a look like the look of one fainting from death", and the other verse supports it: «يَنْظُرون إليك نَظَرَ المَغْشِيِّ عليه من الموت». The third: it is also an adjective of a maṣdar supposed for «تدورُ», that is, "revolving like the revolving of the eye of the one who ...". On both views it is a maṣdar of comparison.
His saying: «سَلَقوكم»: it is said «سَلَقه», that is, he dared against him in his speech, and addressed him in an eloquent address. Its origin is spreading out, and from it «سَلَقَ امرأتَه», that is, he spread her out and had intercourse with her. Musaylima said to Sajāḥ, may Allah the Exalted curse them both:
3684 - ألا هُبِّي إلى المضجَعْ ... فإنْ شِئْتِ سَلَقْنَاك ... وإن شِئْتِ على أربعْ
(Come now to the bed; if you wish we will lay you on your back, and if you wish, on all fours.)
