«السَّليقَةُ» is the natural disposition that comes easily. «السَّليقُ» is the low-lying part of the ground. A speaker is called «مِسْلاق» and «سَلاَّق». It is also said with ṣād. The poet said: 3685 - فَصَلَقْنا في مُرادٍ صَلْقَةً ... وصُداءٍ أَلْحَقَتْهُمْ بالثَّلَلْ
(We struck Murād with a blow, and Ṣudāʾ, which sent them to destruction.)
And «أشحةً» is accusative as a ḥāl from the fāʿil of «سَلَقُوكم». Ibn Abī ʿAbla [reads it] as was said of its sister.

semin-durr:20-20.t:
His saying: {يَحْسَبُونَ}: it may be resumptive, that is, "they are so fearful that they do not believe that the parties have gone away from them". It may also be a ḥāl from one of the pronouns that preceded, if the meaning is sound by that, even if the governing element is remote; so said Abū al-Baqāʾ.
His saying: «بادُوْن»: this is the reading of the majority, the plural of «بادٍ», which is the one residing in the desert. ʿAbd Allāh [Ibn Masʿūd], Ibn ʿAbbās, Ṭalḥa and Ibn Yaʿmar read «بُدَّى» with ḍamma on the bāʾ and doubled dāl, short, like «غازٍ» and «غُزَّى», «سارٍ» and «سُرَّى». It is not analogical; its analogical broken plural is «بُداة» like «قُضاة» and «قاضٍ», but it was carried on the sound form, like their saying «ضُرَّب». A second reading is reported from Ibn ʿAbbās as well, «بَدِيْ» on the pattern of «عَدِي», and a third, «بَدَوْا» as a past verb.
His saying: «يَسْألون»: it may be resumptive, or a ḥāl from the fāʿil of «يَحْسَبُون». The majority read it with sukūn on the sīn followed by a hamza. Ibn ʿAṭiyya reported from Abū ʿAmr and ʿĀṣim transfer of the hamza's vowel to the sīn, as in His saying {سَلْ بني إِسْرَائِيلَ} [al-Baqara: 211]. This is not well known from the two of them; perhaps it was transmitted from them as anomalous, and it is known from al-Ḥasan and al-Aʿmash. Zayd ibn ʿAlī, al-Jaḥdarī, Qatāda and al-Ḥasan read «يَسَّاءَلُون» with a doubled sīn; the origin is «يتساءَلون», which was assimilated, that is, they ask one another.

semin-durr:21-21.t:
His saying: {أُسْوَةٌ}: ʿĀṣim read it with ḍamma on the hamza wherever this word occurs. The others read it with kasra. They are two dialectal forms like «العِدْوَة» and «العُدْوَة», «القِدوة» and «القُدْوَة».
«الأُسْوة» is in the sense of following an example. It is a noun put in the place of the maṣdar, which is «الائْتِساء»; so «الأُسْوة» is to «الائتساء» as «القُدْوة» is to «الاقتداء». It is said «ائْتَسَى فلانٌ بفلانٍ», that is, he followed him. And «أسوةٌ» is the ism of kāna. In the khabar there are two views. The first: it is «لكم», and for the other prepositional phrase several options are possible: attachment to what the khabar is attached to, or to an omitted element as a ḥāl from «أُسْوَة», since had it come later it would have been an adjective, or to «كان» according to one who holds that. The second: the khabar is {فِي رَسُولِ الله}, and «لكم» is as stated above for {فِي رَسُولِ الله}, or it is attached to an omitted element for clarification, that is, "I mean, for you".
His saying: {لِّمَن كَانَ يَرْجُو}: there are several views on it. The first: it is a badal from the kāf in «لكم»; so said al-Zamakhsharī. Abū al-Baqāʾ forbade it, and the Shaykh followed him. Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "It was also said: it is a badal from the pronoun of the addressee with repetition of the preposition. Most forbade it, because the pronoun of the addressee is not substituted." The Shaykh said: "Al-Zamakhsharī said: a badal from «لكم», as in His saying {لِلَّذِينَ استضعفوا لِمَنْ آمَنَ مِنْهُمْ} [al-Aʿrāf: 75]." He said: "It is not permissible according to the school of the majority of the Basrans that a badal that is the whole-for-whole type (badal shayʾ min shayʾ), both being the same entity, be made from the pronoun of the speaker or of the addressee. The Kufans and al-Akhfash allowed that." And he recited:
3686 - بكم قُرَيْشٍ كُفِيْنا كلَّ مُعْضِلَةٍ ... وأَمَّ نَهْجَ الهُدى مَنْ كان ضِلِّيلا
(Through you, O Quraysh, we were spared every difficulty, and he who was lost made for the path of guidance.)
I say: we do not concede that this is a badal of a thing from the same thing, both being one entity; rather it is a badal al-baʿḍ min al-kull (part from whole) in terms of what actually occurs, because the address in His saying «لكم» is broader than {مَن كَانَ يَرْجُو الله} and others, then that generality was specified, because those who actually take him, peace be upon him, as an example are only the believers. What I said is indicated by the apparent likening by al-Zamakhsharī of this verse to the verse of al-Aʿrāf, in which the badal is a whole-for-whole badal. It may be answered: he intended the comparison only in the mere repetition of the governing element.
The second: it is attached to an omitted element as an adjective of «حَسَنةٌ». The third: it is attached to «حَسَنة» itself; both said by Abū al-Baqāʾ. He forbade it to be attached to «أُسْوَة», saying: "because it has already been described." And «كثيراً» means "much remembrance".

semin-durr:22-22.t:
His saying: {وَصَدَقَ الله وَرَسُولُهُ}: it is of the repetition of the explicit noun for glorification, as in his saying: 3687 - لا أرى الموتَ يَسْبِقُ الموتَ شيءٌ ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
(I do not see death, [nor] anything outrunning death ...)
and because, had He repeated them as two pronouns, He would have combined the name of the Creator the Exalted and the name of His messenger in one word, and it would have been said «وصدقا», and the Prophet ﷺ disliked that, and rebuked the one who said it when he said: "Whoever obeys Allah and His Messenger has been guided, and whoever disobeys them both has gone astray." And he said to him: "What a wretched speaker of the people you are. Say: and whoever disobeys Allah and His Messenger", aiming at the glorification of Allah. It was also said: he rebuked him only because he paused at «يَعْصِهما». On the first view, some found a difficulty in his saying, peace be upon him: "until Allah and His Messenger are dearer to him than anything besides them", for he combined them in one pronoun. It was answered: the Prophet ﷺ knows the worth of Allah the Exalted better than we do, so it is not for us to say as he says.
His saying: «وما زادَهُمْ»: the fāʿil of «زادهم» is the pronoun of the promise, that is, "the promise of Allah did not increase them" or truthfulness. Makkī said: "the pronoun of looking, because His saying «لَمَّا رأى» is in the sense of «لَمَّا نظر»." He also said: "It was also said: the pronoun of the seeing, and it was made masculine only because its feminine gender is not real." He did not mention anything other than the two. That is surprising of him, for he restricted what is wide when there was no need.
Ibn Abī ʿAbla read «وما زادُوهم» with a plural pronoun, returning to the parties, because the Prophet ﷺ had told them that the parties would come to them after ten or nine [days].

semin-durr:23-23.t:
His saying: {صَدَقُواْ}: «صَدَقَ» governs two objects, the second with a preposition, which may be omitted. From it is the proverb «صَدَقني سِنَّ بَكْرِهِ» ("he told me the truth about the age of his young camel"), that is, in the age. The verse may be of this kind, with the first omitted, that is, "they were true to Allah in what they covenanted with Allah". It may also govern one object, as you say «صَدَقني زيدٌ وكَذَبني عمرو», that is, he told me the truth and he told me a lie. The thing covenanted upon is then "truthed" figuratively, as if they said to the thing covenanted upon: "We shall fulfil you", and they did. «ما» is in the sense of «الذي»; therefore the pronoun returned to it in «عليه». Makkī said: "«ما» is in the position of accusative by «صَدَقوا». It and the verb form a maṣdar, the implied form being 'they were true to the covenant', that is, they fulfilled it." The return of the pronoun refutes this, except that al-Akhfash and Ibn al-Sarrāj hold that the maṣdar «ما» is a noun.
His saying: «قضى نَحْبَه»: «النَّحْبُ» is what a person committed himself to and resolved to fulfil.
He said:
3688 - عَشِيَّةَ فَرَّ الحارِثيُّون بعدَما ... قضى نَحْبَه في مُلْتَقَى القومِ هَوْبَرُ
(The evening the Ḥārithīs fled after Hawbar had fulfilled his vow at the meeting of the folk.)
And another said:
3689 - بطَخْفَةَ جالَدْنا الملوكَ وخَيْلُنا ... عَشيَّةَ بِسْطامٍ جَرَيْنَ على نَحْبِ
(At Ṭakhfa we battled kings, and our horses, the evening of Bisṭām, ran to a vow.)
that is, to a great matter; therefore it is said «نَحَبَ فلانٌ», that is, he vowed a vow he committed himself to, and death is expressed by it, as in their saying «قَضَى أجله», since death is unavoidable and was made like a thing committed to. «النَّحِيْبُ» is weeping with a voice. «النُّحاب» is coughing.

semin-durr:24-24.t:
His saying: {لِّيَجْزِيَ الله}: there are two views on the lām. The first: it is the lām of cause. The second: it is the lām of consequence. As for what it is attached to, there are several views: either to «صَدَقوا», or to «زادهم», or to «ما بَدَّلُوا». On this al-Zamakhsharī said: "The hypocrites were made as if they intended the evil outcome and willed it by their altering, as the truthful intended the outcome of truthfulness by their fidelity; for both groups are driven to their outcome of reward and punishment, so they are as though equal in seeking and striving to attain them."
His saying: «إنْ شاءَ»: its apodosis is supposed, as is the object of «شاء», that is, "if He wills to punish them, He punishes them". If it is said: their punishment is certain, so how can it be suspended on will, when He has willed to punish them if they die in hypocrisy? Ibn ʿAṭiyya answered: the punishment of the hypocrites is the fruit of their persisting in hypocrisy until their death, and repentance is the counterpart of that persistence, and the fruit of repentance is their being left without punishment; so they are two stations: persistence in hypocrisy, or repentance from it, and from them come two fruits: punishment or mercy. So the Exalted mentioned, by way of concision, one of these two and one of these two, and what was mentioned points to what He left unmentioned. That the meaning of His saying «لِيُعَذِّب» is "to let them continue in hypocrisy" is indicated by His saying «إن شاء» and its balancing with repentance and the particle «أو».
The Shaykh said: "What he mentioned comes to this: the implied form is: 'so that they persist in hypocrisy and die in it, if He wills, then He punishes them, or He turns to them and shows them mercy'. So the cause of punishment was omitted and the effect, which is the punishment, affirmed; and the cause of mercy and forgiveness was affirmed and the effect, which is mercy and forgiveness, omitted."
